rows.claim: The three largest pharmacy benefit managers processed nearly 80% of U.S. prescriptions in 2023 and are tied to major insurers and pharmacies.
rows.limitation: These are interim staff findings, not a Commission ruling, and PBM market shares vary by market segment.
rows.source_words: Federal Trade Commission, Pharmacy Benefit Managers: The Powerful Middlemen Inflating Drug Costs (first interim staff report)

rows.claim: Pharmacies affiliated with the three largest PBMs took in more than $7.3 billion above estimated acquisition cost on 51 specialty generic drugs from 2017 to 2022.
rows.population: Commercial and Medicare Part D plan members
rows.limitation: Revenue above drug acquisition cost, not profit; other pharmacy costs are not subtracted, and it is not a judicial finding.
rows.source_words: Federal Trade Commission, FTC second interim PBM staff report release

rows.claim: The FTC's 2024 complaint alleges the three largest PBMs used rebates that favored high-list-price insulins.
rows.population: People using insulin with commercial coverage
rows.limitation: These are allegations; no court or administrative judge found the companies liable, and the case moved to settlements.
rows.source_words: Federal Trade Commission, FTC sues prescription drug middlemen for artificially inflating insulin drug prices (administrative complaint)

rows.claim: Two insulin cases have proposed settlements and the third was withdrawn from adjudication for a settlement that has not been published; no final FTC order existed for any of them as of October 15, 2026.
rows.limitation: Proposed orders can change before the Commission makes them final, and no data on outcomes for patients exist yet.
rows.source_words: Federal Trade Commission, Caremark and Zinc Health Services: proposed consent order (Federal Register); Federal Trade Commission, FTC, Caremark settlement resolving the insulin case; HealthExec, FTC settles lawsuit with Optum Rx, ending its campaign against the 'big three' PBMs

rows.claim: A 2026 federal law requires PBMs to pass manufacturer rebates through to Medicare drug plans from January 1, 2028, and to employer plans for plan years beginning on or after August 3, 2028.
rows.population: Medicare drug plans and employer group health plans
rows.limitation: Dates come from a law firm summary of Public Law 119-75, and implementing rules are pending.
rows.source_words: Sidley Austin, Congress passes significant federal PBM reform (P.L. 119-75); U.S. Government Publishing Office, Consolidated Appropriations Act,2026, Public Law 119-75

rows.claim: Medicare limits insulin costs to $35 for a one-month supply of each covered insulin, with no deductible.
rows.limitation: Applies to Medicare only; private plans set their own insulin cost sharing unless a state law or settlement applies.
rows.source_words: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (Medicare.gov), Insulin (Medicare coverage)

rows.claim: Out-of-pocket spending on covered Medicare Part D drugs is capped at $2,100 in 2026 and $2,400 in 2027.
rows.limitation: The cap covers drugs on the plan's formulary only; monthly premiums and drugs outside the formulary are separate.
rows.source_words: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (Medicare.gov), Costs for Medicare drug coverage

rows.claim: Medicare has paid negotiated prices for 10 drugs since January 1, 2026; CMS estimated 22% net savings.
rows.limitation: Savings are CMS estimates against prior net prices; the sources do not measure effects on drug development.
rows.source_words: KFF (independent health policy research organization), Key Facts About Medicare Drug Price Negotiation

rows.claim: Negotiated prices for 15 more drugs take effect in 2027 and 15 more, including Part B drugs, in 2028.
rows.limitation: Savings are estimates measured against prior net prices, and third-cycle prices were not final as of October 15, 2026.
rows.source_words: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, CMS Delivers Savings for Seniors on 15 Major Drugs for Cancer and Chronic Disease (press release); KFF (independent health policy research organization), Key Facts About Medicare Drug Price Negotiation

rows.claim: Most drugs that received new patents from 2005 to 2015 were existing drugs.
rows.population: Small-molecule drugs listed in the FDA Orange Book
rows.limitation: A new patent listing does not always delay generic entry; the study counts listings and does not measure price effects.
rows.source_words: Journal of Law and the Biosciences, May Your Drug Price Be Evergreen (Feldman)

rows.claim: Generic competition lowers drug prices, by about 30% with one competitor and nearly 85% with five, according to the FDA.
rows.limitation: Agency summary of its own analyses; effects for biosimilars, which are copies of biologic drugs, are smaller and slower.
rows.source_words: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, Generic Drug Facts
